correctness.rationale: Conditional on a new uniform coordinate pair, all old coordinate pairs produce independent discordance indicators with parameter p=U(1-V)+(1-U)V. Product-uniform change of variables gives exactly f(p)=-log|1-2p| and the normalized beta expectation, cross-checked by three finite formulas. For fixed real s, a beta ratio-of-gammas CLT yields sqrt(n)(2B-1) converging to Z+2s. Uniformly bounded scaled beta densities bound the log singularity near zero, and bounded second moments bound the positive log tails, proving uniform integrability. The Gaussian log expectation at s=0 is -(gamma+log 2)/2. All quantifiers, parity effects and exclusions are explicit; finite checks are not offered as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The pre-existing weak limit has a logarithmic singularity at degree fraction one-half and cannot resolve individual degree masses. Exact finite coefficients and a sharp central width-sqrt(n) crossover identify the natural resolution mechanism and universal Euler-constant offset. The expected central logical type count is of order n log n while fixed noncentral proportions have order n. This is structurally motivated finite-parameter type information and not merely a small-size enumeration.
